# SAR Televenture Limited — SME deep research

Framework v3.0 | Universe position 354 | ISIN INE0PUC01020 | Information cutoff 20 October 2026 | Market reference 19 October 2026

## 1. Executive Verdict

SAR Televenture is a rapidly expanded, acquisition-heavy mix of Indian telecom infrastructure, broadband and UAE fibre-project/equipment services, not a pure tower-rental annuity. Physical deployment and operating profit growth are meaningful positives, and reported financial debt is low. The decisive obstacle is whether the reported earnings, capital deployment and newly changed group perimeter can be reconciled into actual cash available to common shareholders. Primary disclosures show large noncash transactions included in gross cash-flow lines, expired warrant funding, substantial capital advances and a proposed noncash intra-group restructuring. At ₹84.80 the headline historical multiples look low, but that is not a sufficient investment case. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS with explicit mathematical bounds; G2 and G3 are unresolved holds, not findings of fraud or actual default. This is a complex special-situation research candidate, not an evidence-backed compounder. A full cash-flow recast, current pro-forma group balance sheet and funded, billing project economics would change the assessment. [E01–E07]

## 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence

- Legal issuer: SAR Televenture Limited, formerly SAR Televenture Private Limited; NSE Emerge symbol SARTELE, ordinary SM series; ISIN INE0PUC01020. Incorporated in 2019 and listed on 8 November 2023. Do not substitute Tikona Infinet for Tikona Communication, the latter formerly Grand Foundry.
- Price: ₹84.80 official NSE 19 October 2026 closing price, not a live bid or guaranteed execution price. The primary bhavcopy reports 37,000 shares and ₹31,63,425 actual turnover. The 19 October security master and September shareholding filing agree on 50,147,500 shares, face value ₹2 and a 500-share trading lot. Market capitalization is ₹425.2508 crore. An inactive SQ master row carries obsolete capital and is deliberately not used. [E01; market master/bhavcopy]
- Financial scope: consolidated unless expressly described as standalone. FY2021–22 precede the foreign acquisition; FY2023 contains acquired FZE figures; Fusionnet/Parametrique enter thereafter. September 2026 Tikona Communication control is absent from the March 2026 audited financials. It cannot be silently treated as a zero-balance subsidiary.
- Accounting: FY2026 first Ind AS reporting, effective 1 April 2025 with transition date 1 April 2024. Original Indian GAAP accounts, offer-document restatements and later regrouped comparators are retained separately. AS and Ind AS are not assumed equivalent merely because a table labels adjustments nil. [ar26 PDF179–223; audit_inputs]
- Units: ₹ crore unless expressly stated. Original annual notes are usually ₹ lakh; FY2025 AOC1 uses ₹ hundreds. Share counts and price retain their native units. Five-year scenario horizon, ten-year multibagger diagnostic; 15% nominal equity hurdle before personal taxes, separate 16–22% nominal INR WACC sensitivity.

**GOV: 5; Medium confidence.** Mixed stewardship and transparency. No verified severe diversion/minority-abuse finding supports a governance override; financial-reliability hold is separate.

- Original FY24–FY26 statutory opinions and IFC reports read are unmodified; auditor changes around IPO were explained by peer-review eligibility, not an alleged accounting dispute.
- Large share-swap and promoter-loan rights setoff are disclosed; June 2026 monitor explicitly reports warrant expiry and shortfall. Related-party loans and proposed group restructuring require close minority scrutiny.
- Counterevidence: Verified noncash transactions appear inside reported gross cash flow lines, and internal-audit matters remained unresolved at year-end; stewardship is not rated strong.
- Sources: ar24, ar25, ar26, monitor_mar2025, monitor_jun2026.

**MOAT: 4; Medium confidence.** Useful infrastructure access but contestable group economics; scale, customer labels and headline orders do not establish a group-wide moat.

- Domestic tower and FTTH assets can create local right-of-way/installation switching friction and recurring rentals, but SAR is small relative to established tower operators.
- FZE accounted for roughly two thirds of FY26 gross revenue, so tower-network exclusivity cannot be imputed to the entire group; disclosed service-line/retention pricing evidence is insufficient for durable excess economics.
- Counterevidence: An expanding installed base and contracted FTTH/tower relationships are real operating assets, not just a presentation TAM.
- Sources: ar26, business_inputs, peer_inputs.

Missing evidence dominates these small point judgments. Classification remains a hold under either direction, so a 0.1-point apparent cross-company advantage would not be meaningful.

## 4. Business Overview

The listed parent builds and owns small-cell, rooftop/pole and other passive telecom infrastructure, and also participates in FTTH/enterprise network projects. A tower earns attractive incremental economics only after operator acceptance, billing and collections; another paying tenant can leverage a largely existing site. Land rights, power arrangements and technical acceptance matter more than a bare site count. Electricity and land-rent reimbursements can inflate gross revenue without equivalent retained value added. [ipo23; sar_feb2025]

SAR Televenture FZE, previously Shoora International FZE, was acquired on 3 January 2023. It performs fibre deployment/project management and equipment supply/trading in the UAE. Management stated in February 2025 that it did not earn UAE rental income. FZE FY2026 entity turnover was ₹347.8767 crore and PAT ₹51.9733 crore, approximately 66.6% of consolidated revenue and 71.7% of group PAT before elimination/attribution effects. These proportions indicate dependence, not audited segment contribution. The group should therefore not receive an undifferentiated passive-tower annuity multiple. [ar26 AOC1 PDF223; sar_feb2025]

Fusionnet provides broadband/FTTH and connectivity. Parametrique was its wholly owned step-down subsidiary at March 2026; a July internal restructuring proposed direct SAR ownership and conversion of a ₹27.040073 crore loan. Homepasses are premises a network can potentially reach, not paid subscribers. Current active subscriber count, ARPU, churn, paying tenancies, billed site rentals, collected cash per cohort and segment-specific capex are ND in the records reviewed. [ar26; param_acquisition2026; ppt2026]

Revenue recognition policies distinguish usage, subscription/pack validity and activation relationships, but the consolidated annual report reports a single broad tower-related segment despite materially different underlying activities. Cash collection risk consequently differs between concentrated telco rentals, recurring broadband users and UAE project counterparties. A brand-name operator or an MSA is not evidence every site is accepted, fully loaded or collected. [ar26 notes2/21; business_inputs]

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

Mechanism → evidence → durability → failure:

- Local installation and permissions can create switching friction. SAR reports 1,800 FY2026 towers and operator MSAs, while the same presentation introduction says over 1,200. Site acceptance and count reconciliation are missing. Coverage continuity helps, but operator rationalization, competing locations, low tenancy and expiring land agreements can erode the advantage.
- Shared infrastructure can earn high incremental returns with additional paying tenants. SAR does not disclose a current sharing factor or site-level collected revenue. A second tenant is optionality, not an achieved network effect.
- FTTH density can reduce incremental acquisition/servicing costs. Management reports 170,000-plus completed homepasses, with 85,000-plus added in H2. Without paid penetration and churn, it is impossible to tell whether the footprint is an attractive recurring franchise or capital waiting for demand.
- UAE execution capability can win repeat work, but disclosed subcontracting/trading is contestable and current customer concentration, repeat contract share and cash-upstreaming terms are ND. Large contribution from one overseas entity is a concentration exposure, not automatically a moat. [E05]

The economic peer set deliberately spans activities rather than using a telecom-sector label:

| Indus Towers | FY2026: 264,514 towers, 428,014 macro colocations, sharing factor 1.62, revenue ₹32,493cr | Superior-scale network and rental KPI benchmark | Macro/lean mix, customer recovery/provision reversals and lease treatment differ; not a whole-group multiple twin |

Suyog's quarter is not annualized into a false TTM. Indus' disclosed operating FCF definition is not automatically CFO less capex. Peer operating figures establish what good disclosure and monetization look like, not that those securities are cheap. No common-date lease/claim-adjusted peer valuation is asserted. Bharti Hexacom is an active operator, HFCL a product/execution business and Tejas an equipment/IP business; they are adjacent references, not substitutes for the selected economic comparators. [peer_inputs; suyog_q1fy27 PDF3–6/11–12; indus_fy26 PDF1–3; gtpl_fy26 PDF2–4]

Historical domestic concentration is material: Airtel was 100%, 90.06% and 96.05% of FY2021–23 domestic tower revenue respectively. These percentages must not be applied to the later whole group. Current MSAs name Airtel, Vi and BSNL, but current revenue weights are ND. IPO land leases were commonly seven years, extendable three with consent; some were notarized rather than registered. Renewal and enforceability prevent treating all local access as permanent. [ipo23; sar_feb2025]

Reported FY2021–26 CAGR is 256.47%, using ₹0.9071 crore and ₹522.1130 crore over five actual intervals. Reported FY2023–26 CAGR is 152.42%, using ₹32.4617 crore and ₹522.1130 crore over three intervals. Ten-year CAGR is NA because the company was incorporated in 2019. These are mathematical descriptions of a changing entity, not comparable organic demand growth. The measurement policy was selected before scoring: prefer five comparable organic years; use three only if reliable. Neither qualifies, so REV is NS, not a 9 with an invented acquisition haircut. [E02/E05]

FY2023 revenue was already approximately 80.19% acquired FZE contribution: ₹6.4299 crore domestic towers, ₹20.8501 crore fibre projects and ₹5.1817 crore equipment trading. Offer documents also included full-year pre-acquisition profits, with later tax and capital-reserve adjustments. This is a distorted perimeter, not merely a small starting base. Domestic tower growth itself was genuine: 125, 233, 373, 413, 650 and a management-claimed 1,800 at FY2021–26 ends. The conflicting 1,200 figure and absent gross additions/retirements/billing reconciliation limit certainty. [ipo23; fpo24; ppt2026 PDF13]

Entity turnover cross-check: FZE grew from ₹261.8931 crore to ₹347.8767 crore, about 32.8%; Fusionnet from ₹68.1513 crore to ₹132.7316 crore; Parametrique from ₹9.9705 crore to ₹22.4908 crore; parent standalone from ₹35.6343 crore to ₹116.1677 crore. But the parent sold ₹61.503 crore to Fusionnet and ₹22.6158 crore to Parametrique in FY2026, together 72.4% of standalone revenue. Entity sums exceed consolidated revenue by ₹97.1538 crore in FY2026 versus approximately ₹25.7191 crore in FY2025. Those differences are arithmetic residuals, not a verified elimination schedule. They cannot establish organic growth or be counted as additional group sales. [ar25 AOC1, ar26 PDF162/223]

Latest available complete annual period is FY2026. The May 2026 presentation reports H2 revenue ₹280.35 crore versus ₹207.21 crore, 35.3% growth, and PAT ₹36.22 crore versus ₹28.52 crore. Annual audited revenue less rounded H2 gives indicative H1 ₹241.7630 crore versus ₹142.7201 crore. This is an explicit derived approximate bridge, not independently audited half-year extraction, and prior H1 acquired Fusionnet only from August 2024. PPT FY2025 PAT/PBT also differ slightly from the audited annual figures. No FY2027 half-year result or invented TTM is inserted at this cutoff. Current momentum is positive but does not fix the constant-scope gap. [ppt2026 PDF22, printed slide21; ar26]

## 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway

The domestic runway is plausible, but access, commissioning, paid utilization and financing must be separated. IPO budgets contemplated 300 additional towers at ₹12.39 crore including GST, approximately ₹4.13 lakh per site. The 2024 expansion budget contemplated 1,000 towers at ₹42.5 crore, approximately ₹4.25 lakh each, and 300,000 homepasses at ₹273 crore, ₹9,100 per homepass. These are dated budgets, not verified current capex or cost per paying subscriber. A 300,000-homepass network at 20% paid conversion has 60,000 users; at 40% it has 120,000. Without SAR ARPU, churn, maintenance, channel and collection costs, neither number establishes attractive incremental cash returns. [ipo23; fundraise2024]

Bottom-up diagnostic only: from 1,800 management-claimed sites, 300 annual net additions would reach 3,300 in five years; at the old ₹4.25 lakh budget, that is ₹63.75 crore tower capex before escalations, maintenance, site working capital and capacity mix. Completing the remaining 130,000 of the 300,000 homepass goal would represent ₹118.3 crore at the original ₹9,100 budget, but much earlier funding sits in vendor advances, so that amount must not be simply added to current commitments. The actual remaining payable requires project-by-project advance/deployment reconciliation. These simple units test feasibility, not a new forecast or accessible market-share claim. [A; E05]

Funding is central. At March 2026 capital advances are ₹228.4494 crore and optical-fibre commitments net of advances ₹75.0914 crore. The June monitoring report separately discusses a ₹120 crore fibre leasing/maintenance MOU without contract terms, counterparties, duration or overlap with that commitment. All unexercised warrants expired on 11 May 2026. The agency reports ₹98.36 crore received/utilized versus a planned ₹172.79 crore and explicitly says the shortfall affects the stated objects' viability. Nil deviation in application does not mean all financing was raised or physical sites were commissioned. [ar26 note36; monitor_jun2026 PDF4/7/15/18]

The cash model therefore never assumes the missing ₹74.4 crore exercise money arrives. It separately funds the disclosed net capital commitment, noncash deployment of already-funded advances, incremental capacity, maintenance, working capital and growing operating reserves. Hypothetical bank/equity support is capped and fee-bearing. No base-case dividend coexists with unfunded growth. Mature cash economics and a current acquisition balance sheet remain unavailable, so CAP/CASH/BAL and consequently GQS are NS; the missing-evidence rule is more appropriate than a low-score growth override.

## 8. Management, Governance & Execution

The share-capital history explains why business growth is not the same as per-share growth. Split-adjusted closing shares were approximately 0.2025m in FY2021, 0.20875m in FY2022 and 3.2643m in FY2023, versus 15m after the IPO, 47.1075m in FY2025, 49.5475m in March 2026 and 50.1475m currently. The June 2023 5-for-1 split itself is not economic dilution. Loan conversions, the 1:1 rights issue, FPO, acquisition shares and warrant conversions are genuine changes in common claims. [financial_inputs capital_history]

The 2024 composite ₹450 crore was not ₹450 crore new cash: the monitor identifies ₹225.87 crore promoter unsecured loans adjusted into rights capital and ₹224.13 crore received in the monitoring account. Fusionnet consideration was approximately ₹241.209586 crore, largely 9,965,000 SAR shares at ₹242 plus ₹0.056586 crore cash. FY2025 annual notes explicitly say no cash was received for those swap shares. Converting a disclosed promoter loan or acquiring an asset with shares is not by itself abusive; treating these transactions as cash financing in a model would nevertheless be wrong. [ar25 note1; ar24 AGM material; monitor_mar2025]

## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

The most important variable is actual collected, parent-attributable operating cash after all project commitments, not reported revenue growth. The linked bear path is slower UAE execution/collections or domestic billing acceptance → lower margins and larger receivables/supplier advances → more project completion/maintenance cash → exhausted available cash and no expired-warrant rescue → adverse borrowing/new equity or stalled capacity → impaired goodwill/advance recovery and reduced common value. Subsequent group restructuring can further separate consolidated profit from parent-common ownership. [E03–E07]

The strongest favorable counterargument is that assets funded in advance can mature, the domestic footprint has grown, FZE earned substantial profit, conventional debt is very small, and all issues may ultimately be reconcilable presentation/noncash timing rather than missing money. That would materially improve the thesis. The current work does not deny it; it requires proof through collected cash, counterparties, commissioning and pro-forma claims. The share-swap and promoter setoff are openly disclosed, not discovered secret dealings. Unmodified audit opinions and the absence of a reported default are meaningful counterevidence.

Permanent-loss risk is High/uncertain, not a precisely calibrated probability: recoverability of capital advances/goodwill, funding of commitments and common-claim dilution are material. A price decline alone is not permanent loss. The conditional bear valuation quantifies a severe earning-power outcome only when its assumed finance survives; failed-funding paths have no ordinary shareholder recovery quote. No statistical success probability is invented. The market may already recognize complex accounting and acquisition risk, but a low multiple or past price fall does not establish a differentiated bargain.

SAR's acquisitions, pre-acquisition profits, uneven EPS denominators and current common/preference structure weaken a clean historical identity, so the enterprise/common-claim bridge is used instead. A hypothetical 5x or 10x group operating value does not imply 5x or 10x per-share wealth. Future public cash needed for growth, unfavorable issuance prices, NCI and terminal reinvestment can absorb it. No current accessible market-share evidence supports the highest tested growth rates.

## 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action

Classification: Hold — unresolved financial reliability and current funding/perimeter. Research priority, not eligible for a favorable investment conclusion. No buy/sell recommendation, position allocation or trade is implied.

The v3.0 matrix requires final point scores; incomplete BQS/GQS/IAS must not be forced into its numerical cells. There is no compounder designation: the required scores, governance/moat/revenue/capital thresholds, confidence and clear critical gates are not established. Unknowns are not scored zero and the company is not placed last as if proven poor. G2/G3 holds should be displayed separately from investable rankings, with the actual reason. [judgments; E06]

A lower price alone cannot resolve the capital/cash/perimeter questions. It changes conditional modeled returns, not historical BQS/GQS evidence. A credible cash-flow recast, actual current obligations/funding, funded paid-site/customer cohorts, and a pro-forma common/preference claim reconciliation can change the decision. Confirmed serious misconduct would justify a different and stronger conclusion; this report does not assume it.

## 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown: SAR Televenture is a rapidly expanded, acquisition-heavy mix of Indian telecom infrastructure, broadband and UAE fibre-project/equipment services, not a pure tower-rental annuity. Physical deployment and operating profit growth are meaningful positives, and reported financial debt is low. The decisive obstacle is whether the reported earnings, capital deployment and newly changed group perimeter can be reconciled into actual cash available to common shareholders. Primary disclosures show large noncash transactions included in gross cash-flow lines, expired warrant funding, substantial capital advances and a proposed noncash intra-group restructuring. At ₹84.80 the headline historical multiples look low, but that is not a sufficient investment case. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS with explicit mathematical bounds; G2 and G3 are unresolved holds, not findings of fraud or actual default. This is a complex special-situation research candidate, not an evidence-backed compounder. A full cash-flow recast, current pro-forma group balance sheet and funded, billing project economics would change the assessment. [E01–E07]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
The listed parent builds and owns small-cell, rooftop/pole and other passive telecom infrastructure, and also participates in FTTH/enterprise network projects. A tower earns attractive incremental economics only after operator acceptance, billing and collections; another paying tenant can leverage a largely existing site. Land rights, power arrangements and technical acceptance matter more than a bare site count. Electricity and land-rent reimbursements can inflate gross revenue without equivalent retained value added. [ipo23; sar_feb2025]

SAR Televenture FZE, previously Shoora International FZE, was acquired on 3 January 2023. It performs fibre deployment/project management and equipment supply/trading in the UAE. Management stated in February 2025 that it did not earn UAE rental income. FZE FY2026 entity turnover was ₹347.8767 crore and PAT ₹51.9733 crore, approximately 66.6% of consolidated revenue and 71.7% of group PAT before elimination/attribution effects. These proportions indicate dependence, not audited segment contribution. The group should therefore not receive an undifferentiated passive-tower annuity multiple. [ar26 AOC1 PDF223; sar_feb2025]

Fusionnet provides broadband/FTTH and connectivity. Parametrique was its wholly owned step-down subsidiary at March 2026; a July internal restructuring proposed direct SAR ownership and conversion of a ₹27.040073 crore loan. Homepasses are premises a network can potentially reach, not paid subscribers. Current active subscriber count, ARPU, churn, paying tenancies, billed site rentals, collected cash per cohort and segment-specific capex are ND in the records reviewed. [ar26; param_acquisition2026; ppt2026]

Revenue recognition policies distinguish usage, subscription/pack validity and activation relationships, but the consolidated annual report reports a single broad tower-related segment despite materially different underlying activities. Cash collection risk consequently differs between concentrated telco rentals, recurring broadband users and UAE project counterparties. A brand-name operator or an MSA is not evidence every site is accepted, fully loaded or collected. [ar26 notes2/21; business_inputs]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.content_markdown:
Mechanism → evidence → durability → failure:

- Local installation and permissions can create switching friction. SAR reports 1,800 FY2026 towers and operator MSAs, while the same presentation introduction says over 1,200. Site acceptance and count reconciliation are missing. Coverage continuity helps, but operator rationalization, competing locations, low tenancy and expiring land agreements can erode the advantage.
- Shared infrastructure can earn high incremental returns with additional paying tenants. SAR does not disclose a current sharing factor or site-level collected revenue. A second tenant is optionality, not an achieved network effect.
- FTTH density can reduce incremental acquisition/servicing costs. Management reports 170,000-plus completed homepasses, with 85,000-plus added in H2. Without paid penetration and churn, it is impossible to tell whether the footprint is an attractive recurring franchise or capital waiting for demand.
- UAE execution capability can win repeat work, but disclosed subcontracting/trading is contestable and current customer concentration, repeat contract share and cash-upstreaming terms are ND. Large contribution from one overseas entity is a concentration exposure, not automatically a moat. [E05]

The economic peer set deliberately spans activities rather than using a telecom-sector label:

| Suyog Telematics | June 2026 quarter: 6,103 towers, 7,468 tenancies, ₹70.9cr revenue, ₹42cr EBITDA; monthly site revenue excluding electricity ₹31,000–31,500 | Billing tenancy, operator mix and site economics | Different mix/scale; April 2026 grossing of electricity reimbursements changed reported revenue/margins; no normalization into SAR |

| GTPL Hathway broadband | FY2026: ₹558cr broadband revenue, about 2% growth, 1.06m active users, 5.95m homepasses, ARPU ₹465 | Paid conversion, retention and monetization | Cable-heavy parent and different geography; calculated 17.8% active/homepass ratio is not a forecast for SAR |

Suyog's quarter is not annualized into a false TTM. Indus' disclosed operating FCF definition is not automatically CFO less capex. Peer operating figures establish what good disclosure and monetization look like, not that those securities are cheap. No common-date lease/claim-adjusted peer valuation is asserted. Bharti Hexacom is an active operator, HFCL a product/execution business and Tejas an equipment/IP business; they are adjacent references, not substitutes for the selected economic comparators. Historical domestic concentration is material: Airtel was 100%, 90.06% and 96.05% of FY2021–23 domestic tower revenue respectively. These percentages must not be applied to the later whole group. Current MSAs name Airtel, Vi and BSNL, but current revenue weights are ND. IPO land leases were commonly seven years, extendable three with consent; some were notarized rather than registered. Renewal and enforceability prevent treating all local access as permanent. [ipo23; sar_feb2025]

Offer documents also included full-year pre-acquisition profits, with later tax and capital-reserve adjustments. This is a distorted perimeter, not merely a small starting base. Domestic tower growth itself was genuine: 125, 233, 373, 413, 650 and a management-claimed 1,800 at FY2021–26 ends. The conflicting 1,200 figure and absent gross additions/retirements/billing reconciliation limit certainty. [ipo23; fpo24; ppt2026 PDF13]

Entity turnover cross-check: FZE grew from ₹261.8931 crore to ₹347.8767 crore, about 32.8%; Fusionnet from ₹68.1513 crore to ₹132.7316 crore; Parametrique from ₹9.9705 crore to ₹22.4908 crore; parent standalone from ₹35.6343 crore to ₹116.1677 crore. But the parent sold ₹61.503 crore to Fusionnet and ₹22.6158 crore to Parametrique in FY2026, together 72.4% of standalone revenue. Entity sums exceed consolidated revenue by ₹97.1538 crore in FY2026 versus approximately ₹25.7191 crore in FY2025. Those differences are arithmetic residuals, not a verified elimination schedule. They cannot establish organic growth or be counted as additional group sales. [ar25 AOC1, ar26 PDF162/223]

Latest available complete annual period is FY2026. The May 2026 presentation reports H2 revenue ₹280.35 crore versus ₹207.21 crore, 35.3% growth, and PAT ₹36.22 crore versus ₹28.52 crore. Annual audited revenue less rounded H2 gives indicative H1 ₹241.7630 crore versus ₹142.7201 crore. This is an explicit derived approximate bridge, not independently audited half-year extraction, and prior H1 acquired Fusionnet only from August 2024. PPT FY2025 PAT/PBT also differ slightly from the audited annual figures. No FY2027 half-year result or invented TTM is inserted at this cutoff. Current momentum is positive but does not fix the constant-scope gap. [ppt2026 PDF22, printed slide21; ar26]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.content_markdown:
The domestic runway is plausible, but access, commissioning, paid utilization and financing must be separated. IPO budgets contemplated 300 additional towers at ₹12.39 crore including GST, approximately ₹4.13 lakh per site. The 2024 expansion budget contemplated 1,000 towers at ₹42.5 crore, approximately ₹4.25 lakh each, and 300,000 homepasses at ₹273 crore, ₹9,100 per homepass. These are dated budgets, not verified current capex or cost per paying subscriber. A 300,000-homepass network at 20% paid conversion has 60,000 users; at 40% it has 120,000. Without SAR ARPU, churn, maintenance, channel and collection costs, neither number establishes attractive incremental cash returns. [ipo23; fundraise2024]

Bottom-up diagnostic only: from 1,800 management-claimed sites, 300 annual net additions would reach 3,300 in five years; at the old ₹4.25 lakh budget, that is ₹63.75 crore tower capex before escalations, maintenance, site working capital and capacity mix. Completing the remaining 130,000 of the 300,000 homepass goal would represent ₹118.3 crore at the original ₹9,100 budget, but much earlier funding sits in vendor advances, so that amount must not be simply added to current commitments. The actual remaining payable requires project-by-project advance/deployment reconciliation. These simple units test feasibility, not a new forecast or accessible market-share claim. [A; E05]

Funding is central. At March 2026 capital advances are ₹228.4494 crore and optical-fibre commitments net of advances ₹75.0914 crore. The June monitoring report separately discusses a ₹120 crore fibre leasing/maintenance MOU without contract terms, counterparties, duration or overlap with that commitment. All unexercised warrants expired on 11 May 2026. The agency reports ₹98.36 crore received/utilized versus a planned ₹172.79 crore and explicitly says the shortfall affects the stated objects' viability. Nil deviation in application does not mean all financing was raised or physical sites were commissioned. [ar26 note36; monitor_jun2026 PDF4/7/15/18]

The cash model therefore never assumes the missing ₹74.4 crore exercise money arrives. It separately funds the disclosed net capital commitment, noncash deployment of already-funded advances, incremental capacity, maintenance, working capital and growing operating reserves. Hypothetical bank/equity support is capped and fee-bearing. No base-case dividend coexists with unfunded growth. Mature cash economics and a current acquisition balance sheet remain unavailable, so CAP/CASH/BAL and consequently GQS are NS; the missing-evidence rule is more appropriate than a low-score growth override.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.content_markdown:
The share-capital history explains why business growth is not the same as per-share growth. Split-adjusted closing shares were approximately 0.2025m in FY2021, 0.20875m in FY2022 and 3.2643m in FY2023, versus 15m after the IPO, 47.1075m in FY2025, 49.5475m in March 2026 and 50.1475m currently. The June 2023 5-for-1 split itself is not economic dilution. Loan conversions, the 1:1 rights issue, FPO, acquisition shares and warrant conversions are genuine changes in common claims. [financial_inputs capital_history]

The 2024 composite ₹450 crore was not ₹450 crore new cash: the monitor identifies ₹225.87 crore promoter unsecured loans adjusted into rights capital and ₹224.13 crore received in the monitoring account. Fusionnet consideration was approximately ₹241.209586 crore, largely 9,965,000 SAR shares at ₹242 plus ₹0.056586 crore cash. FY2025 annual notes explicitly say no cash was received for those swap shares. Converting a disclosed promoter loan or acquiring an asset with shares is not by itself abusive; treating these transactions as cash financing in a model would nevertheless be wrong. [ar25 note1; ar24 AGM material; monitor_mar2025]

| Composite proceeds monitoring, March 2025 | Reports all ₹450cr utilized; ₹34.90cr expenses; ₹9.73cr cheque timing into Q1FY2026 | Spending/accounting completion is not operating commissioning or customer collection |

| 1 October Fusionnet transfer | Proposed ₹256.84cr entirely in 3.20% cumulative redeemable preference shares, ten-year redemption | Not cash monetization, subject to approvals; exact voting deadline is not relied upon here |

September shareholding primary evidence reports promoters 22,833,225 shares, 45.53%; public 27,314,275, 54.47%. M.G. Metalloy holds 21,233,225 and Sanidhya Garg 1,600,000. Promoter encumbrances are reported nil. Locked promoter shares are 6,028,571 and locked public shares 469,500; public holding is not the same as freely offered orderbook supply. No outstanding warrants, convertibles or ESOPs are shown. These facts are favorable against an assumption of hidden existing dilution, but do not guarantee future shareholder treatment. [primary September SHP, business_inputs]

RPT examination includes ₹177.90 crore FY2024 promoter financing, later loan setoff, subsidiary loans and the new restructuring. FY2026 standalone CARO identifies loans during the year ₹52.83 crore, closing Fusionnet ₹45.6631 crore and Parametrique ₹27.1980 crore, plus ₹15 crore Fusionnet equity investment. Consolidated current related-party loans ₹2.8539 crore are not clearly mapped to counterparties in the RPT closing schedule. Other loans and interest-bearing advances require recovery/terms evidence. Reported KMP remuneration/professional fees include Vikas ₹0.3190 crore, Deepak ₹0.4799 crore and Pankaj ₹1.0560 crore, approximately ₹1.8549 crore combined, not itself disproportionate proof of misconduct. Management's ordinary-course/arm's-length assertion is attributed, not independently validated. [ar26 PDF120–123/200/217]

Auditor continuity is nuanced. Raheja resigned in July 2023 because of peer-review certificate eligibility; Dharit Mehta's January 2024 change was similarly described. Original FY2024 CARO and FPO differ on exact Raheja reappointment date. FY2024–26 original opinions and IFC reports reviewed are unmodified; original FY2021–23 reports remain ND, though offer examinations identify audit dates and no qualifications requiring restatement. FY2026 internal audit had some unresolved matters without quantified nature. Edit-log operation/no tampering is reported in the relevant audits, with scope/preservation wording differences retained in audit_inputs. None is automatically fraud, and a clean opinion does not erase the specific numerical issues below. [audit_inputs; original audit page locators in source register]

### What is resolved, and what remains material

Resolved FY2025 presentation differences include ₹1.4934 crore tax assets netted against tax provisions, ₹6.4948 crore deposits moved out of cash equivalents, and approximately ₹34.9584 crore reserves relabeled with unchanged equity. CFO/CFF regrouping of roughly ₹3.6643 crore largely explains their comparator difference. These are not unexplained losses. FY2023 PAT increased ₹0.0523 crore through an explicit tax correction. A separate small equity bridge residual and changes to pre-acquisition profit allocation remain visible. [audit_inputs reconciliation]

Material unresolved cash-flow items:

1. FY2025 gross equity proceeds ₹691.1455 crore equal ₹449.9925 crore composite issuance plus ₹241.1530 crore noncash Fusionnet swap. The composite itself includes ₹225.87 crore promoter-debt setoff. Approximately ₹467.023 crore is therefore noncash; residual fresh-cash proxy ₹224.1225 crore agrees with the rounded monitor ₹224.13 crore. The matching debt repayment and acquisition lines also need adjustment. Removing noncash equity alone would corrupt the cash bridge.

FY2026 CFO includes a large other-assets movement; subtracting the ₹125.0657 crore advance-balance reduction from reported CFO gives a classification-only proxy of negative ₹4.0011 crore. This is not verified actual CFO: advances may have moved noncash into PPE, and acquisitions/FX also matter. Conversely earlier negative CFO partly financed capital advances, not necessarily delinquent customer payments.
3. The PPE cash line approximately equals tangible additions less disposed net book value, while a separate ₹16.4751 crore CWIP reduction is treated as investing inflow. Commissioning can be noncash. Reported goodwill purchase equals goodwill balances/movements, not necessarily cash purchase consideration net of acquired cash. The full transfer/acquisition/cash schedule is ND.
4. FY2026 cash FX adjustment ₹18.5211 crore equals the entire translation OCI. Cash changed by negative ₹3.9080 crore versus negative ₹22.4291 crore before that adjustment. A bank-by-currency cash reconciliation is required; equality alone does not prove the cash balance false.
5. FY2026 issue transaction cost ₹34.4869 crore is large versus ₹44.286 crore incremental warrant conversion cash. Earlier monitoring reports ₹34.90 crore composite expenses and cheque timing, so it must not all be described as fees on the FY2026 conversion. Actual expense/payment allocation remains unresolved.
6. Borrowing interest is paid in financing; interest income is not stripped from CFO; lease principal is not separately clear. The FY2025 gratuity comparative ₹0.5770 crore versus note provision ₹0.0527 crore, an incomplete cost-of-services note and ageing redistribution are additional lower-materiality control questions, not separate allegations. FY2026 receivables ₹164.8131 crore grew faster than revenue; average receivable days are 83.920 versus ending days 115.218, compared with FY2025 ending 78.513. The denominator is total revenue, a disclosed credit-sales proxy. Supplier advances ₹78.3654 crore, inventories ₹29.7958 crore, GST ₹38.1712 crore and deferred/unclaimed ITC ₹6.2156 crore are cash uses/assets, not liquid funding. Project/services cost-based inventory/payable days are only secondary proxies, not a universal manufacturing CCC. [metrics working_capital; ar26 notes9–11]

Gross receivables ageing includes ₹4.4842 crore 6–12 months overdue, ₹0.6237 crore 1–2 years, ₹0.3509 crore 2–3 years and ₹1.5527 crore over three years; ECL is ₹0.2113 crore. That is not a claim every balance is impaired. FY2025 ageing originally put all receivables below six months, while the later comparator redistributes ₹5.7255 crore to older buckets. Obtain customer schedules and subsequent receipts rather than assuming the new ageing means sudden new defaults. [ar25/ar26 ageing; audit_inputs]

Cash equivalents are ₹12.3292 crore. Other deposits ₹2.9107 crore include lien FDs ₹0.5936 crore; escrow ₹0.50 crore is separate. The model excludes all other deposits until availability is verified, not just restricted portions, and never subtracts restricted cash twice from the cash-equivalent line. Loans ₹17.0274 crore and accrued interest ₹1.9611 crore are not counted as available cash. Financial debt ₹1.4413 crore plus leases ₹0.2221 crore gives signed reported net debt ₹-10.6658 crore; this mixed-date figure says nothing about the full September acquisition's obligations. Contingencies include ₹0.5736 crore bank guarantees, ₹0.2220 crore license exposure and ₹1.2674 crore GST show-cause amount. A show-cause notice is not an established loss; the bear case tests payment. Deferred tax is not described as due tomorrow. [ar26 notes17–20/36; model_inputs]

Gross loans/advances/goodwill, stale claims and instrument rights prevent calling P/B an asset floor. Reported FCF yield is negative and classification-limited. [metrics indicative_valuation]

The preferred eventual method is a sum of separately supported cash streams: collected UAE projects, accepted/billing tower cohorts, paying broadband cohorts, and the current parent common/preference claims. Those data are not yet complete. A frozen-perimeter monthly FCFF diagnostic plus EBIT-multiple cross-check is still useful to identify assumptions and funding failures, but not to manufacture R or IAS.

Model basis: ₹522.113 crore bridge annual pace, then five-year growth 0%/10%/20% for bear/base/bull with a 20% bear demand shock; operating EBITDA margins 12%/17.5%/20%; DSO 150/115/90; normalized tax 25.17%/15%/15%; terminal WACC 22%/19%/16%, growth 2%/3%/4%, and EBIT multiples 6/8/10. These are analyst scenarios, not management guidance. Terminal growth is below WACC. The model reflects existing assets and committed capital; site-count calculations above are a reality check, not an unsupported segment-to-sales equality.

The ₹75.0914 crore disclosed net commitment is paid over assumed 24 months; ₹228.4494 crore already-funded advances deploy over 36 months noncash into PPE, with 2.5% additional completion cash and a 25% sensitivity. Baseline growth needs ₹0.35 fixed investment per incremental rupee of revenue; maintenance is the greater of 2.5% revenue and 4% asset replacement, and D&A is separately modeled. Receivables, inventories, supplier/GST balances and operating cash reserves all increase with sales. No cash-free growth is assumed.

Known May warrant cash ₹10.89 crore is offset by reported downstream MOU payments, not left as free parent cash. MOU overlap with recurring costs/capital commitments is unknown; the baseline treats it as additional project spending and a full-overlap sensitivity removes the incremental duplicate budget assumption. This is not an assertion the MOU is a new ₹120 crore legally due obligation; contractual commitment and remaining payments are unresolved. No second group cash outflow is recorded for the internal parent loan. [monitor_jun2026; model_spec]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
The most important variable is actual collected, parent-attributable operating cash after all project commitments, not reported revenue growth. The linked bear path is slower UAE execution/collections or domestic billing acceptance → lower margins and larger receivables/supplier advances → more project completion/maintenance cash → exhausted available cash and no expired-warrant rescue → adverse borrowing/new equity or stalled capacity → impaired goodwill/advance recovery and reduced common value. Subsequent group restructuring can further separate consolidated profit from parent-common ownership. [E03–E07]

The strongest favorable counterargument is that assets funded in advance can mature, the domestic footprint has grown, FZE earned substantial profit, conventional debt is very small, and all issues may ultimately be reconcilable presentation/noncash timing rather than missing money. That would materially improve the thesis. The current work does not deny it; it requires proof through collected cash, counterparties, commissioning and pro-forma claims. The share-swap and promoter setoff are openly disclosed, not discovered secret dealings. Unmodified audit opinions and the absence of a reported default are meaningful counterevidence.

Permanent-loss risk is High/uncertain, not a precisely calibrated probability: recoverability of capital advances/goodwill, funding of commitments and common-claim dilution are material. A price decline alone is not permanent loss. The conditional bear valuation quantifies a severe earning-power outcome only when its assumed finance survives; failed-funding paths have no ordinary shareholder recovery quote. No statistical success probability is invented. The market may already recognize complex accounting and acquisition risk, but a low multiple or past price fall does not establish a differentiated bargain.

G2.reason: Verified noncash share-swap and debtsetoff appear in grosscash flow proceeds; corresponding acquisition/debt/capital advance/FX cash bridges remain incomplete. Unmodified audits do not resolve this analytical contradiction.
G2.reopen: Issuer/auditor reconciled cash flow statements, noncash transaction schedule, subsidiary/currency cash bridge and corrected EPS/share denominators.

G3.reason: Expired warrants leave no future exercise cash. Material commitments and newly controlled Tikona lack a current funded pro forma. Diagnostic financing failures are not actual defaults.
G3.reopen: Current bank cash/restrictions, dated committedfinance, project payments, and consolidated post-acquisition claim/survival bridge.

G4.reason: Primary 60-session actual trading supports reference-position capacity; lot granularity, spread/depth and circuit execution still constrain practical exit.
G4.reopen: Current brokerorderbook/restrictions and intendedposition size before execution.
